lines.text: July, 1518. A woman began dancing in a Strasbourg street... and seemingly couldn't stop.
lines.tts: July, fifteen eighteen. A woman began dancing in a Strasbourg street... and seemingly, couldn't stop.

lines.text: A crowded city, already worn down by hunger and disease.
lines.tts: A crowded city, already worn down by hunger and disease.

lines.text: Within a week, dozens had joined her. Some accounts say hundreds, by August.
lines.tts: Within a week, dozens had joined her. Some accounts say hundreds, by August.

lines.text: The council turned to physicians. Their verdict: a natural illness, caused by hot blood.
lines.tts: The council turned to physicians. Their verdict: a natural illness, caused by hot blood.

lines.text: Their cure? More dancing. Halls were cleared, a stage was built, and musicians were hired.
lines.tts: Their cure? More dancing. Halls were cleared, a stage was built, and musicians were hired.

lines.text: It only seemed to spread. So the council banned public dancing.
lines.tts: It only seemed to spread. So the council banned public dancing.

lines.text: Many feared a curse of Saint Vitus. Modern theories range from mass psychogenic illness... to toxic, mouldy grain.
lines.tts: Many feared a curse of Saint Vitus. Modern theories range from mass psychogenic illness... to toxic, mouldy grain.

lines.text: In the end, the dancers were taken to a shrine of Saint Vitus, in the hills, to pray for healing.
lines.tts: In the end, the dancers were taken to a shrine of Saint Vitus, in the hills, to pray for healing.

lines.text: By September, the dancing had faded. Five centuries later, historians still debate what really happened.
